11. While it has come on record that accused Aman Mathur was driving car Toyota Liva at the time of incident, what remains to be proved is whether the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.

The words 'rash' and 'negligent' have not been defined in IPC but there are numerous precedents wherein their meaning and import has been clarified.

It has been observed in several cases that 'criminal rashness is doing a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so and may cause injury but without intention to cause injury and without knowledge that injury would probably be caused'.
Thus, to incur criminal liability, act must be done with rashness or indifference as to the consequences.
State Vs.
Aman Mathur Samiksha Gupta FIR No. 158/2022, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Gupta

Date: Page No.13 o  2024.02.15  16:36:04 -0200 Criminal negligence is gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise reasonable care and proper precaution imperative to be adopted by a person to avoid causing injury to the public or individual.

A question whether the accused's conduct amounted to culpable rashness or negligence depends directly on the question as to what is the amount of care and circumspection which a prudent man would consider to be sufficient.
12. In the present case, the evidence of prosecution rests on the testimony of injured/complainant PW1/Radhey Shyam Thakur and eyewitness PW2 Santosh Kumar.

As per prosecution version,
complainant was driving the motorcycle with PW Santosh who was riding pillion and the incident took place while he was going from Shahbad Mohammadpur Railway crossing to Sector 8 Dwarka.
When he reached outside D-21 Corporate Park, accused came out of the said Corporate Park, driving his car at a high speed and hit the complainant's bike, causing them to fall down.

Per contra, it is the version of accused that complainant was going from Sector 8 Dwarka towards Shahbad Mohammadpur railway crossing and accused was going to the Corporate Park to pick his father from office.

On reaching the entrance of Corporate Park, accused had given right indicator in order to enter D-21 Corporate Park and the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of complainant, who tried to overtake the car of accused, while it was in an almost stationery position.
The said version of accused is evident from his testimony and the cross examination of complainant conducted by counsel for accused.

sentences.text: Perusal of testimony of PW Radhey Shyam and Santosh shows that their evidence is riddled with various inconsistencies.

During his initial statement to the police on which basis FIR was registered,
PW Radhey Shyam had stated that he had called PCR after the incident.
He also stated that after the accident, accused got out of his car, looked at them and left the spot.
These facts were reiterated by him during the examination in chief.
However, during his cross examination, he stated that PCR call was made by his brother in law Santosh after the incident.

He also stated that after the incident,
accused got down from his car and asked him if any assistance was required.

During the evidence of PW Santosh Kumar, he asserted that he had called PCR after the incident,
thus creating doubt on the prosecution version.
He also stated that accused went away after the incident without offering to help.
There is yet another contradiction in the version of Pws (both of whom were present at the time of incident, which version is disputed by the accused).
PW Radhey Shyam has stated that guards present outside the gate of D 21 Corporate Park came forward to help him, after the incident.

However, PW Santosh has deposed that while 2-3 guards were present outside the Corporate Park,
no one came to help them.

sentences.text: However, PW Santosh has testified that after PW Radhey Shyam got medical help, they returned to their home and police officials visited him in the evening to record his statement.

Similarly, PW Radhey Shyam has testified during his cross examination that father of accused was present with him in the car at the time of incident, which was not mentioned by him in his original complaint to the police.
However, PW Santosh has testified during his cross examination that father of accused was not present with him in the car at the time of incident.
Considering such contradictions, the testimony of IO ASI Kamal Singh assumes significance.
Perusal, however, of the same, shows that investigation conducted by the IO is faulty and lackadaisical.
The date of incident is 24.03.2022.

However,
offending car in question was seized by the IO only on 31.03.2022.
This delay in proceedings allow for scope of tampering with the case property.
IO has stated that neither accused nor injured was found at the spot when he reached and therefore inquiry was done from passersby.
If this was the case, then, what precluded the IO from recording their statements is something to be explained by the prosecution.
It has come on record that guards were present outside the gate of D 21 Corporate Park.
However, IO did not conduct inquiry from such important witnesses for reasons best known to him.
IO did not collect the CCTV footage of the place of incident and this significant omission can only benefit the accused.
IO has also admitted that site plan was prepared by him at the instructions of complainant and he did not conduct any independent inquiry to verify such version of complainant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, accused has placed pictures and videos to show the entry and exit points of D 21 Corporate Park.
It is clear from the video that there were speedbreakers right at the entrance of the Corporate Park.
Thus, the probability that accused was driving his car at a high speed is bleak.
It is here that the investigation done by IO as to rashness and negligence in driving could have been material.
However, since proper investigation has not been done, the charge against the accused cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
These facts deposed during prosecution evidence clearly suggest that criminal rashness or negligence while driving the car cannot be pinned on the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, it is difficult to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accident took place due to negligent driving of the accused.
Thus, the prosecution has failed to substantiate the charge U/s 279 IPC against the accused and in the event of such failure, charge U/s 338 IPC against accused also remains unsubstantiated.

The words 'rash' and 'negligent' have not been defined in IPC but there are numerous precedents wherein their meaning and import has been clarified.
It has been observed in several cases that 'criminal rashness is doing a dangerous or wanton act with the knowledge that it is so and may cause injury but without intention to cause injury and without knowledge that injury would probably be caused'.
Thus, to incur criminal liability, act must be done with rashness or indifference as to the consequences.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The evidence of prosecution witnesses in the present case has to be examined against this legal position.
12. In the present case, the evidence of prosecution rests on the testimony of injured/complainant PW1/Radhey Shyam Thakur and eyewitness PW2 Santosh Kumar.
As per prosecution version,
complainant was driving the motorcycle with PW Santosh who was riding pillion and the incident took place while he was going from Shahbad Mohammadpur Railway crossing to Sector 8 Dwarka.
When he reached outside D-21 Corporate Park, accused came out of the said Corporate Park, driving his car at a high speed and hit the complainant's bike, causing them to fall down.
On reaching the entrance of Corporate Park, accused had given right indicator in order to enter D-21 Corporate Park and the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of complainant, who tried to overtake the car of accused, while it was in an almost stationery position.
The date of incident is 24.03.2022.
However,
offending car in question was seized by the IO only on 31.03.2022.
This delay in proceedings allow for scope of tampering with the case property.
IO has stated that neither accused nor injured was found at the spot when he reached and therefore inquiry was done from passersby.
If this was the case, then, what precluded the IO from recording their statements is something to be explained by the prosecution.
It has come on record that guards were present outside the gate of D 21 Corporate Park.
However, IO did not conduct inquiry from such important witnesses for reasons best known to him.
IO did not collect the CCTV footage of the place of incident and this significant omission can only benefit the accused.
IO has also admitted that site plan was prepared by him at the instructions of complainant and he did not conduct any independent inquiry to verify such version of complainant.
On the other hand, accused has placed pictures and videos to show the entry and exit points of D 21 Corporate Park.
It is clear from the video that there were speedbreakers right at the entrance of the Corporate Park.
Thus, the probability that accused was driving his car at a high speed is bleak.
It is here that the investigation done by IO as to rashness and negligence in driving could have been material.
However, since proper investigation has not been done, the charge against the accused cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
These facts deposed during prosecution evidence clearly suggest that criminal rashness or negligence while driving the car cannot be pinned on the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, it is difficult to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accident took place due to negligent driving of the accused.
Thus, the prosecution has failed to substantiate the charge U/s 279 IPC against the accused and in the event of such failure, charge U/s 338 IPC against accused also remains unsubstantiated.
opennyai_summary.decision: Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, accused Aman Mathur is entitled to benefit of doubt and is therefore acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
